turns.doctor_question: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi Dr. Smith. Um, I'm here because I just can't stop thinking about my face. The left side of it, specifically. It looks really crooked and... just messed up. 

It's constantly on my mind. Whenever I'm at work at the warehouse, or even if I try to go out to salsa night, I just feel like everyone is staring at it and noticing how off it is. People tell me they don't see anything when I bring it up, but I know what I see, and I just can't stop fixating on it. It's really taking a toll on me.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes persistent preoccupation and fixation on a perceived defect in their face (crookedness) that others report not seeing.

turns.doctor_question: When people tell you they don't notice anything different about your face, is there any part of you that considers they might be right, or are you completely certain that your face really is crooked and messed up?
turns.patient_response:
Honestly... no. I don't think they're right at all. I mean, I look in the mirror, and it's just... it's right there. The left side is definitely crooked. I'm completely certain about it. 

When people tell me they don't notice it, I just figure they're trying to be polite, or maybe they just don't want to make me feel bad. But I know what I'm looking at. It really is messed up.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from your concerns about your face, have you noticed any other unusual beliefs or experiences—like feeling people are plotting against you, or hearing/seeing things others don't?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't have anything like that. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there, and I don't think anyone is plotting against me. It's really just... just my face that I'm dealing with. That's the only thing that's bothering me.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient explicitly denies persecutory or unusual beliefs, stating they do not think anyone is plotting against them.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient clearly denies hallucinations, stating they do not hear voices or see things that are not there.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself doing certain things repeatedly because of how your face looks—like checking it in mirrors, trying to cover or fix that side of your face, or asking others to reassure you about it?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I do. Especially at work. Before I go back out on the inventory floor, I always end up in the bathroom checking the mirror. I just keep looking at it, trying to pull my cap down a certain way to hide it, or rubbing at the left side of my face like I can somehow fix it. 

I get stuck doing it. Sometimes I'm in there so long that I end up late getting back out, and my picking numbers fall way behind. My boss has been getting on my case about it a lot lately. But I just can't stop checking it.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient explicitly confirms engaging in repetitive behaviors in response to appearance concerns, including repeatedly checking the mirror, camouflaging with a cap, and rubbing at their face.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from concerns about how your face looks, have you had any other fixed beliefs about your body—like something being wrong internally, a foul smell, or a bodily function not working right?
turns.patient_response: No, nothing like that. I don't... I don't think I smell bad or have anything wrong on the inside. Everything else with my body works fine. It really is just my face. That's the only thing I'm worried about.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient reaffirms their appearance concern, stating that their face is the only thing they are worried about.
symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient explicitly denies having fixed beliefs about internal physical illness, bodily malfunction, or foul odors.
